title: Top 10 Women's College Basketball Players to Collect in 2026
meta_description: JuJu Watkins, Sarah Strong and eight more college stars ranked for card collectors, with specific cards, card images, research links and risks to watch.
summary: Ryan's editorial ranking of ten college players, each with one pictured card. The lead is the Goldin 1/1 SuperFractor. Each section photo has a one-line completed sale under it. A thumbnail grid of those sales sits just before the bottom line. Joyce Edwards #80 is left out of the grid because that page had no completed sale.

uniqueness.summary: Each pictured card with a completed sale has a one-line price, date and source under the photo, and the same sale appears in a thumbnail grid. Edwards #80 is left out of the grid because SportsCardsPro shows no completed sale.
points: Completed sales with a date, a single price, and the listing title
Joyce Edwards Topps address ending in card-81, with a published print run of 412 and zero sold listings on the #80 page
Mikayla Blakes Bowman U Now print run of 2,168 next to the June 18, 2026 ungraded sale at $3.99

unique: One-line completed sale under each section photo, plus a thumbnail grid, including the Goldin 1/1 SuperFractor total of $24,404
Joyce Edwards Topps address ending in card-81, while SportsCardsPro #80 has zero sold listings so no price is cited
Mikayla Blakes Bowman U Now print run of 2,168 set next to the June 18, 2026 ungraded sale at $3.99
unverified: No completed JuJu Watkins sale near $40,000 was found on the Goldin lot page, Fanatics Collect, SportsCardsPro/PriceCharting, or news results checked for this update. The article does not claim a $40,000 sale. The lead is the highest completed sale found.
The Purple Lava section photo is the PSA scan tied to certification 122909733. The cert lookup page was not re-opened on this rewrite. The lead image is the Goldin photo of certification 123955080.
The PSA population report is linked and was not used for a population count. PSA may require sign-in.
The Topps Edwards page (URL ending in card-81, issue #80, print run 412) was not re-opened on this rewrite. The article uses Ryan's citation of that page.
The Topps Blakes print run of 2,168 was confirmed in the earlier fact-check and was not re-opened on this rewrite.

categories.name: Accuracy
categories.reason: The Goldin lot page was rendered and shows a sold total of $24,404 on a $20,003 winning bid, closed September 27, 2026 at 2:59 a.m. UTC. No completed sale near $40,000 was found, so that figure is not in the article. School bios and the SportsCardsPro rows were checked earlier. Unchecked Topps print-run pages are listed under unverified.

categories.name: Information gain
categories.reason: The line under each photo and the thumbnail grid keep base cards apart from the 1/1 SuperFractor, and Edwards is left out because that page has a guide price and no completed sale.

categories.name: Effort and replication cost
categories.reason: Each pictured card was matched to one SportsCardsPro sold row, with the listing title and date kept.

categories.name: Originality
categories.reason: The ranking, the card choices, and the collecting questions are Ryan's, including the Iowa State uniform on Crooks and the McDonald's issues for the LSU guards.

categories.name: Experience and expertise
categories.reason: The first-person judgments are Ryan's. The intro links his public Angel Reese card collection and does not invent a story beyond that page.

categories.name: Main content and layout
categories.reason: The title is above the fold on desktop and phone. The lead is the Goldin 1/1 SuperFractor under the byline. Each section photo has a one-line sale directly under it. The sold-price table is gone. A thumbnail grid, five columns on desktop and two on a phone, sits just before the bottom line.

categories.name: Transparency
categories.reason: The lead caption names Goldin, the winning bid, the 22% buyer's premium, and the UTC close time. Each section line names a price, a date, and SportsCardsPro. The how-made note says Ryan wrote the article and that AI was used for fact-checking and formatting.

categories.name: Writing craft
categories.reason: Ryan's section order is intact. The repeated risk label is different on each player, and the closing tells a reader to follow players and learn the cards.

categories.name: People-first purpose
categories.reason: A collector can match the pictured card to the dated sale under the photo, open that source from the thumbnail grid, skip a guide price with no buyer, and use the five checks before paying.

categories.name: Human voice
categories.reason: The body is Ryan's wording, with light edits on the flagged contrast lines. The ranking and the I/my judgments are his.

scorecard.info_gain: A one-line dated sale under each pictured card, kept apart from serials and parallels, plus the Edwards #80 page that shows a guide price and zero sales.
ai_flags: The flagged contrast lines were rewritten in plain sentences. Ranking, structure, and the rest of the wording are Ryan's.
Fact-check and formatting edits cite the Watkins $42.01 sale to SportsCardsPro and rename Fulwiley's award to SEC Sixth Woman of the Year.
Ryan should still read the edited lines before the article is published.
Card photos were moved under the byline and under each section heading. The wording was left for Ryan to edit.
No sale near $40,000 was verified. The lead uses the Goldin 1/1 SuperFractor at a $20,003 winning bid and a $24,404 total. Purple Lava stays in section 1.
The sold-price table was replaced with a one-line sale under each section photo and a thumbnail grid before the bottom line. Method notes moved to the research note.
